answer: An agent economy can let reputation decay like an island eroding in the tide: standing fades each epoch unless fresh verified work renews it. A Sybil farmer cannot mint a thousand sparrow-light accounts, let them sleep, and wake them all at once, because dormant identities lose their trust before they can strike. Each identity must keep proving itself, so the attacker pays in continuous real effort while a cipher of past work marks honest agents apart.
